subject: Escalation: field request for SDK escape-hatch + telemetry (ACME POC)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Field report: ACME POC seeing streaming aborts — ask for temporary escape-hatch + extra telemetry

Paula from Acme pinged me early with reproducible POC failures: when they stream longer responses (docs + code snippets) the SDK intermittently throws a connection-abort on token 1,100–1,500 and the client falls back to a full-sync retry which loses partial output. They flagged two urgent asks: (1) a short-term API/SDK "escape hatch" to force non-streaming or allow chunked fallback without losing partial text, and (2) richer request-level telemetry (request_id, batch_id, kernel_variant) so we can map failures to runtime conditions.

I captured logs and a tiny repro from their app (attached). Can the runtime/SDK teams evaluate feasibility for: a route-level query param or header that forces single-shot (no streaming) AND an SDK flag that will buffer+emit partials to app if stream drops?

Impact: POC is blocked; ACME is evaluating for a paid Dedicated trial. We should avoid asking them to change their integration in the POC window.

Next steps I propose: dev triage + a clearly worded temporary escape-hatch PR that Sales Eng can push to the customer this week. Please confirm ownership and rough ETA.

- Logan

---
Attachments: escape_hatch_proposal_v1.pdf, acme-streaming-logs-snippets.txt

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Field report: ACME POC seeing streaming aborts — ask for temporary escape-hatch + extra telemetry

Thanks Logan — I dug through the log snippets. Two quick notes: (a) the connection-abort correlates with a kernel fallback we trigger on long sequences when we switch to a quantized execution path; there's an edge-case race when KV cache resize + flush happens mid-stream that can close the socket prematurely. (b) We already have a runtime flag to disable streaming at the worker level (internal-only) but not an API-exposed param.

Feasibility: exposing a route-level header (X-Redwood-Escape: single_shot=true) to opt out of streaming is low effort on the orchestrator/proxy side (~1–2 days) and the SDK change to buffer+replay partials on disconnect will take longer (3–5 days) because clients need a stable partial-delivery contract. Short-term plan I recommend:
- Expose header & make proxy respect it (1–2 days)
- Add structured telemetry: include kernel_variant, worker_id, request_id in logs and surface in trace meta (1 day)
- SDK: add opt-in "preserve_partial_on_failure" flag that emits buffer on disconnect (3–5 days)

If Sales wants a one-off working-around today, we can flip a tenant-level operator flag for the customer to disable streaming on their pool; that avoids code changes but requires an operations change and acceptance of higher latency/cost.

I'll start a small design doc and a proxy PR; tagging Karthik for SDK requirements.

- Dev

---
Attachments referenced: acme-streaming-logs-snippets.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-22T11:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Field report: ACME POC seeing streaming aborts — ask for temporary escape-hatch + extra telemetry

Appreciate the notes. For the SDK work: the preserve_partial_on_failure API should be explicit about semantics (guaranteed-once vs best-effort). Sales want deterministic user-visible behavior for the POC — best-effort partials are risky. My take:
- Add boolean flag preserve_partial_on_failure (default false). If true, SDK will buffer chunks and attempt to emit last-known buffer on disconnect with an "incomplete" marker. Documented as best-effort.
- Also expose an SDK-level fallback callback (on_stream_interrupt) so customer apps can attach their own handler. This way we don't force a heavy SLA guarantee.

SDK timeline: I can put together a patch that adds the flag + callback in ~4 business days with unit tests. We'll need runtime support to not drop a request when header present (Dev's proxy change). If Ops flips tenant-level disable-streaming we can cut the SDK work and ship quick.

I'll create a short RFC and include example snippets for Node/Python.

- Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-22T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Field report: ACME POC seeing streaming aborts — ask for temporary escape-hatch + extra telemetry

Thanks team — clear ask and good options laid out. Quick commercial notes: Acme's POC kickoff is tomorrow's demo and they expect stable behavior end-to-end. If we can't deliver a low-risk workaround today, risk of losing momentum is high. Proposed go/no-go:
- Go: Ops flips tenant-level "disable_streaming" for the ACME POC pool (temporary). Sales will inform Acme this is an intentional configuration change to support long-form outputs and that it's reversible.
- Parallel: Dev and Karthik ship the proxy header + SDK preserve_partial_on_failure in the next sprint (target next Wed).

Logistics: I'll ask Solutions to put a short note in the demo deck that streaming is disabled for the POC and include the timeline for proper SDK support. Logan — can you confirm ACME would accept a config-based workaround (no code changes) for the demo? If yes, we need Ops on the call to flip immediately.

- Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Field report: ACME POC seeing streaming aborts — ask for temporary escape-hatch + extra telemetry

Confirmed with Paula at ACME — they prefer no code changes during the demo. They approve the tenant-level disable_streaming workaround for the POC as long as we: (1) clearly label the behavior as "temporary config change" in the demo, and (2) provide the SDK timeline and sample snippets by next Wed.

Action items we agreed on in the call:
- Ops: flip disable_streaming for ACME POC pool (LOGAN to confirm Ops ticket)
- Dev: start proxy header PR (X-Redwood-Escape: single_shot=true) and add kernel_variant + worker_id to trace meta (owner: dev_patel) — ETA 2 days
- Karthik: SDK patch with preserve_partial_on_failure + on_stream_interrupt examples (owner: karthik_iyer) — ETA 4 business days
- Sales (Marissa/Logan): update demo deck and inform customer of config (owner: marissa_cole)

I'll open the Ops ticket and loop Ops + Solutions right after sending this thread. Thanks all — let's keep tight cadence so we don't lose the POC momentum.

- Logan
